A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain corresponding main sections, appendices A–E, three tables, and six figures. The text and visual material support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations of fictitious-play variants in Section 5 and Appendix E, including regret trajectories and means and standard deviations over 100 random initializations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulation results in Section 5 and Appendix E, including Tables 2–3 and Figures 1 and 4–6.

M1.justification: The optimistic and alternating fictitious-play update rules and tiebreaking provisions are unchanged. The Appendix B correction concerns an analytical reduction, not the algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Matching Pennies and the same identity, generalized Rock-Paper-Scissors, and uniformly random payoff-matrix families, retaining the 15×15, 25×25, and 50×50 settings.

E2.justification: Standard FP remains the comparator to OFP in Tables 2–3 and Figures 4–6. Figure 1 retains standard FP and alternating FP alongside OFP; no evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Both retain 10,000 iterations, the same fixed and random initializations, lexicographical and randomized tiebreaking, and the 2/3 payoff scaling for RPS trajectory plots.

E4.justification: Appendix E retains the same checks of robustness to tiebreaking and initialization. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Tables 2–3 continue to report means and standard deviations over 100 random initializations. No run-count, seed, or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 contain identical values, and the empirical curves in Figures 1 and 4–6 are unchanged. For example, Table 2 reports 15×15 identity-game regret of 155.1±3.9 for FP and 8.1±1.6 for OFP in both versions.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 corrects the matrix shift from A + [det(A)/(a+b-c-d)] times the all-ones matrix to A - [det(A)/(a+d-b-c)] times that matrix. This repairs the determinant-zero construction in Proposition 4.1; the theorem statements and overall proof framework remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both retain the constant-regret guarantee for OFP in 2×2 games with a unique interior equilibrium, the alternating-FP lower bound on Matching Pennies, and the empirical suggestion of constant regret in higher dimensions.

C2.justification: v2 labels the existing higher-dimensional open question as Limitations and adds a generic broader-impact statement. Neither introduces a substantive new interpretation, applicability boundary, or limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 newly states that experimental code is in supplementary material and that all experiments ran locally on one personal computer. These are additional disclosures; the supplied PDFs do not verify the supplementary code's availability.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the relationship to regularized optimistic FTRL, earlier fictitious-play research, and learning in 2×2 games.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited front-matter and prose edits, adds Limitations and Broader impact labels and accompanying text, and expands Appendix E.1. The section organization and nearly all existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts NeurIPS formatting throughout, changing typography, spacing, and the title and author layout. Table 1 changes placement, and appendix Figures 4–6 are resized and redistributed across pages. All three tables and six figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 repairs the algebraic error in the determinant-zero reduction in Appendix B.1 and adds limited reproducibility information in Appendix E.1. These are useful, localized improvements; the central guarantees, experimental evidence, and unresolved higher-dimensional question remain unchanged.
